add.title: Nthabiseng Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre and Others, Case No. 2024/070075 - High Court of South Africa, Gauteng Local Division, Johannesburg (Fisher J), judgment of 10 November 2025
add.summary: The only documented determination of where trans prisoners are housed in Gauteng. Mokoena, a transgender woman serving life, is held at Johannesburg Correctional Centre: initially housed in Medium A section where she could express her gender identity (long hair, makeup, women's clothing); later transferred to Medium C section; at the time of the judgment she was housed in C Single Section, a segregated/solitary-confinement unit of Medium C, and - despite requesting a single cell - was accommodated with cisgender male cellmates (first two cisgender gay men, then one cisgender male), which DCS justified by overcrowding. The court found the DCS's SOPs prescribe accommodation appropriate to gender identity where feasible and safe and that no basis existed for refusing single accommodation, ordering DCS to house her in a single cell or with inmates of the same gender identity and to enforce its transgender-inmate SOPs.

add.title: Media Statement: National Preventive Mechanism welcomes the High Court ruling affirming the rights of transgender persons in correctional facilities
add.summary: SAHRC (as South Africa's OPCAT National Preventive Mechanism) welcomes the 10 November 2025 judgment of the Gauteng Division of the High Court, Johannesburg, in Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (Case No. 2024/070075), which found the DCS engaged in unfair discrimination and harassment of transgender inmate Nthabiseng Mokoena - including by failing to provide appropriate accommodation - and ordered the DCS to enforce its SOPs on transgender inmates and house her in a single cell or with inmates of the same gender identity. Confirms the Correctional Services Act vulnerable-inmate accommodation framework as the operative housing standard in Gauteng's correctional centres.
